atoms.1: A non-reactive result for the Hepatitis A IgM (Immunoglobulin M) antibody test indicates that the individual does not have a recent or current Hepatitis A infection.
atoms.2: IgM antibodies are typically produced in response to a recent infection.
atoms.3: The presence of IgM antibodies usually indicates an acute or recent infection.
atoms.4: A non-reactive result suggests that the individual may have been vaccinated against Hepatitis A.
atoms.5: A non-reactive result suggests that the individual has a past infection that is no longer active.
atoms.6: A non-reactive result suggests that the individual has never been infected with the Hepatitis A virus.
atoms.7: A non-reactive result does not necessarily rule out a past infection.
atoms.8: IgM antibodies may not be detectable after a certain period.
atoms.9: To confirm the status of Hepatitis A immunity, a Hepatitis A IgG (Immunoglobulin G) antibody test may be performed.
atoms.10: A Hepatitis A IgG antibody test can detect antibodies that provide long-term immunity.

snippets.output: A non-reactive result for the Hepatitis A IgM (Immunoglobulin M) antibody test indicates that the individual does not have a recent or current Hepatitis A infection.
IgM antibodies are typically produced in response to a recent infection.
The presence of Hepatitis A IgM antibodies usually indicates an acute or recent Hepatitis A infection.

A non-reactive Hepatitis A IgM result suggests that the individual may have been vaccinated against Hepatitis A, had a past Hepatitis A infection that is no longer active, or has never been infected with the Hepatitis A virus.
A non-reactive Hepatitis A IgM result does not necessarily rule out a past Hepatitis A infection, because IgM antibodies may not be detectable after a certain period.
To confirm the status of Hepatitis A infection/immunity, a Hepatitis A IgG (Immunoglobulin G) antibody test may be performed.
A Hepatitis A IgG antibody test can detect antibodies that provide long-term immunity.
